content.text: Digital [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-how-creators-ghana-get-paid-online-complete-4|How to]] face significant barriers when traditional payment platforms like Stripe or PayPal are unavailable, especially in regions like Nigeria or Venezuela. COREMERCH provides a robust solution with a sovereign commerce [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-automated-ebook-delivery-after-crypto-10|infrastructure]] that eliminates these barriers. This guide details how to use Supabase as your order database for a digital store, ensuring seamless crypto payment acceptance without relying on conventional platforms.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The sovereign commerce infrastructure is designed to provide resilience against the limitations of traditional payment processors. By leveraging tools like [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-first-3|COREMERCH guide to github]] Pages and Supabase, you gain full ownership of your digital store without dependence on third-party services. This approach ensures that you can operate your business independently, circumventing the restrictions imposed by platforms that often exclude creators in specific regions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, gather the necessary components for your infrastructure. You'll need a GitHub account for hosting your website, access to Supabase for managing your order database, and a NOWPayments account for processing crypto transactions. Familiarize yourself with the Sovereign Blueprint, as it outlines the steps you'll follow during deployment. A good internet connection and basic programming knowledge will also facilitate a smoother setup.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, begin by configuring Supabase as your order database. Create tables for tracking customer orders, and ensure that your NOWPayments account is linked for crypto payment verification. Once these components are in place, you can use Google Apps Script to automate order confirmations and product delivery. This ensures that customers receive their digital products instantly after payment is confirmed, enhancing their purchasing experience.
Gain full ownership of your digital store infrastructure.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After setting up your infrastructure, it's time to go live. Deploy your website on GitHub Pages and ensure all configurations are correct. Test your payment processing by completing a transaction using a small amount of cryptocurrency. Monitor the process via your order database in Supabase to confirm that payments are processed correctly and that customers receive their products. This hands-on approach will help you troubleshoot any issues before promoting your store more widely.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is operational, consider scaling your digital store by adding more products and optimizing your marketing strategies. Leverage Supabase's capabilities to analyze customer behavior and improve your offerings based on insights gained from data. You can also explore the Edge Commerce Stack for more advanced features, ensuring your business can grow sustainably while maintaining the security and independence of your operations.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
No dependency on third-party platforms means greater freedom.

The setup decision comes down to time versus depth. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything to build Stack 01 yourself in an afternoon or Stack 02 over a weekend — full source code, step-by-step configuration, and the NOWPayments integration guide. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH build Stack 02 for you in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured for email deliverability. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. Both are at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.
